explanation: Interpret the signed input as its 32-bit unsigned bit pattern. Clearing the lowest set bit removes one 1 at a time, so the number of iterations equals the requested population count, including negative inputs.
timeComplexity: O(s), where s≤32 is the number of set bits
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: For a nonzero unsigned bit pattern, x&(x−1) clears exactly its lowest set bit and leaves all other set bits unchanged. Counting these reductions until zero therefore equals the original 32-bit population count. Casting preserves negative inputs’ two’s-complement pattern.
walkthrough: The signed value −2147483648 has bit pattern 10000000000000000000000000000000. One reduction clears its single set bit, so the answer is 1.
edgeCases: An unsigned working value avoids arithmetic-shift loops on negatives.
